mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% month-over-month indicates an acceleration in economic output, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) where PAYEMS rises while RSAFS falls by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand relative to income, which reduces corporate sales and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0% and RSAFS < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages indicates a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA and FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above 5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and labor and supports corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the median return is not significantly above zero at 90% confidence.
